seoTitle: How to Assign Tasks in Google Workspace via Google Chat
metaDescription: Learn how to assign tasks to teammates directly inside Google Chat using Google Workspace's built-in Tasks integration and smart chips.
intro: Switching between a chat window and a separate task manager slows a team down and buries action items in message threads nobody rereads. Google Workspace solves this by building task assignment straight into Google Chat spaces, so a task created in a conversation shows up with an owner, a status, and a due date without anyone leaving the chat. This guide walks through opening a Chat space, finding the Tasks tab that most people never notice, and assigning work so it's tracked instead of just mentioned. It works the same whether you're in the standalone Chat app or the Chat panel inside Gmail, and it applies to Business Starter, Standard, and Education accounts alike.

steps.heading: Get to Google Chat from your Workspace apps
steps.body: If you're already in the Google Admin console or another Workspace app, the fastest route into Chat is the app grid in the top-right corner — click it and choose Chat alongside Gmail, Drive, and Calendar. Admins managing a domain will recognize this launcher; regular users can also just go to chat.google.com or open the Chat icon inside Gmail's left sidebar. Either path lands you in the same Chat interface, so use whichever is fewer clicks from where you already are.

image.caption: The Google Workspace app launcher, with Chat sitting next to Gmail, Drive, and Calendar as one of the core apps in the suite.

steps.heading: Open the space where the task belongs
steps.body: Tasks in Chat live inside a space, not a one-off direct message, so start by opening (or creating) the space your team already uses — something like a named project or team space rather than a private DM. A brand-new space shows a welcome prompt with quick-start buttons for Add members, Share a file, and Assign tasks; that Assign tasks button is the shortcut into the flow this guide covers. On an established space you'll skip the welcome card and go straight to the Tasks tab described next.

image.caption: A Chat space right after creation, with quick-start buttons for adding members, sharing a file, and assigning tasks.

steps.heading: Switch to the Tasks tab
steps.body: Every space has a Tasks tab next to Chat and Shared at the top of the window — this is the piece most people miss because it looks like just another tab rather than a project tracker. Click it and you'll see a simple table: Title, Date, and Assignee as columns, with any existing tasks already listed. This view is shared by everyone in the space, so a task added here is visible to the whole team immediately, not just the person who created it.

image.caption: The Tasks tab inside a space, showing a task with its title, due date, and an "Assigned to you" label next to the assignee.

steps.heading: Create the task and set a due date
steps.body: Click Add a space task, type a clear, specific title — vague titles like "follow up" get ignored, while "Send Q3 report draft to client" doesn't — and set a due date from the Date column so the deadline is visible without anyone having to ask. You can also create a task inline from a chat message using the smart chip that appears when you type an @ mention followed by task-related text, which is handy when the task grows naturally out of a conversation instead of being planned in advance.

steps.heading: Assign it to the right person
steps.body: Click the Assignee column and pick a member of the space; the task then appears both in the shared Tasks tab and in that person's personal Google Tasks list, so they see it even outside of Chat. The list in this guide's example shows a task already tagged "Assigned to you," which is exactly the confirmation you're looking for — it means the task is now tracked against a specific person rather than floating as an unassigned to-do that everyone assumes someone else will handle.

steps.heading: Track progress without leaving the conversation
steps.body: As work gets done, whoever owns the task checks it off directly in the Tasks tab, and that status is visible to the whole space in real time. This is the actual payoff of the feature: instead of a manager pinging "any update on this?" in the chat thread, anyone can glance at the Tasks tab and see exactly what's open, what's assigned to whom, and what's already checked off — accountability built into the same window where the work was discussed in the first place.

faq.question: Do I need a specific Google Workspace plan to assign tasks in Chat?
faq.answer: This feature works across Business Starter, Standard, and Education accounts, though exact availability can vary by plan.

faq.question: Can I assign tasks in Google Chat from the Gmail interface too?
faq.answer: Yes, since Google Chat is integrated into Gmail, you can access and assign tasks from either the Gmail sidebar or the standalone Chat app.

faq.question: Do tasks assigned in a Chat space work the same as a direct message?
faq.answer: No — the Tasks tab and the space task list are features of named spaces, not one-on-one direct messages. Create or use a team space if you want a shared, trackable task list.

faq.question: Will the assigned person get a notification?
faq.answer: Yes, assigning a task typically triggers a notification so the person knows a new task has been added to their list.

faq.question: Can I set recurring tasks through Google Chat?
faq.answer: The basic assignment flow covers one-time tasks with due dates; more advanced recurring task setups may require Google Tasks directly.
